claim: An AAAI-25 accepted calibration paper evaluated its method across 9 reasoning datasets and multiple open- and closed-source LLM families in a single paper.
stance_target: scope expected of an AAAI-accepted calibration paper
scope_conditions: LLM confidence calibration via sampling-based consistency measures, reasoning QA tasks
quoted_support: We perform an extensive evaluation across various open and closed-source models on nine reasoning datasets.

claim: Instruction-tuning makes LLM calibration harder, while model scale, sample size, and intermediate explanations improve it.
quoted_support: factors such as intermediate explanations, model scaling, and larger sample sizes enhance calibration, while instruction-tuning makes calibration more difficult

claim: Consistency-based (sampling-derived) calibration methods outperform existing post-hoc calibration approaches for LLMs.
quoted_support: Results show that consistency-based calibration methods outperform existing post-hoc approaches.

claim: The paper's arXiv 'Comments' field says 'AAAI 2024' while the AAAI Digital Library / ACM listing places it in the Proceedings of the Thirty-Ninth AAAI Conference (AAAI-25), indicating authors sometimes label the venue by decision year rather than conference year.
stance_target: how to interpret AAAI year labels on arXiv comment fields

claim: Confidence scores derived from sample consistency can be used to improve model accuracy (e.g., via selection/voting), not merely to report reliability.
quoted_support: confidence scores obtained from consistency have the potential to enhance model performance
